title: bound-windowed-attention-replay
summary: Bound replay or prefill query rows across a producer/consumer boundary whose retained inputs and separately preserved historical state satisfy the full dependency closure. Use when a model has shared hidden state or preserved-compressed KV and the retained region must be derived rather than assumed. Derives the retain rule from window plus rollback depth, separates query-row compaction from dropping historical keys, and names what becomes unrecoverable.

skill_metadata.name: bound-windowed-attention-replay
skill_metadata.description: Bound replay or prefill query rows across a producer/consumer boundary whose retained inputs and separately preserved historical state satisfy the full dependency closure. Use when a model has shared hidden state or preserved-compressed KV and the retained region must be derived rather than assumed. Derives the retain rule from window plus rollback depth, separates query-row compaction from dropping historical keys, and names what becomes unrecoverable.

applicability.scope: Decoders with an explicit producer/consumer boundary and a demonstrated dependency closure for compact query rows, including separately preserved historical state
applicability.prerequisites: A derived dependency closure; a full-length KV write at the boundary; known rollback depth; control over metadata construction
applicability.hardware: Backend-independent retain arithmetic; window sizes, boundary index and ring lengths come from the model config and do not transfer
applicability.input_contract: The actual producer/consumer split and transitive dependency closure, boundary index, window and rollback depth, consumer KV sharing/compression layout and separately preserved historical keys.
applicability.produced_artifact: A dependency listing, enforced retain length, compact query/position/store-slot/visibility metadata, a separate historical-key retention statement and a diagnostic equivalence-reference mode.
applicability.failure_modes: Applying window-plus-rollback without dependency closure, discarding full-layout state, clipping away the sampling row, or comparing across preemption can invalidate replay; compact queries do not imply historical keys were dropped.
applicability.refusal_point: Stop if required consumer state is unavailable without a preserved full-length copy, the boundary representation cannot be captured, or comparison preemption moves the anchor. Do not use for clipped-region outputs or required bit-identical preemption replay.

limitations: Source-derived candidate; no equivalence run was performed.
Applies to architectures with a demonstrated boundary dependency, not to arbitrary sliding-window stacks.
Window sizes, boundary-layer index and ring lengths are model-config specific and are not transferable.
Query-row compaction does not imply dropping historical keys; the two decisions are separate.
Prompt logprobs are unrecoverable for the clipped region; the reference forces them off with a warning.
The truncation path is off by default in the reference source.
recommendations: Derive every consumer dependency before computing keep; preserve the required full-layout representation separately from the compact query rows.
Use the visibility-only diagnostic mode to isolate equivalence from row gathering, and retain one sampling row for a fully clipped chunk.
Check metadata at chunk/store boundaries, actual prompt-logprob handling and zero preemption during equivalence comparison.
